text: Kristin Otto, born on 7 February 1966 in Leipzig, Bezirk Leipzig (present-day Sachsen), East Germany, is a former East German swimmer who became an Olympic, World, and European champion multiple times. She is most renowned for being the first woman to win six gold medals at a single Olympic Games, achieved at the 1988 Seoul Olympic Games. In long course swimming, she held world records in the 100 meter and 200 meter freestyle events. She was also the first woman to swim the short course 100 meter backstroke in under a minute, accomplishing this at an international short course meet at Indiana University in 1983. Otto began swimming at age 11 in an East German sports academy and competed in her first world championships in 1982, winning a gold medal in the 100 meter backstroke and two additional golds in the 4×100 m relays. After 1982, she changed coaches and focused on speed strokes; at the 1983 European Championships, she finished second in the 100 meter freestyle behind Birgit Meineke. In 1984, she set a world record in the 200 meter freestyle but was unable to compete at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics due to the boycott by 14 Eastern Bloc countries, including East Germany. In 1985, she fractured a vertebra, which prevented her from competing for most of the year or attending the European Championships. She returned in 1986 at the World Championships in Madrid, winning four gold medals (100 m freestyle, 200 m individual medley, 4×100 m medley relay, and 4×100 m freestyle relay) and two silver medals (50 m freestyle, 100 m butterfly), and continued her success at the 1987 European Championships, where she won five gold medals. At the 1988 Seoul Olympics, she won six gold medals and set Olympic records in the 50 m freestyle and 100 m butterfly. Otto retired from swimming in 1989 and currently works as a sports reporter for German television. She was named Female World Swimmer of the Year by Swimming World in 1984, 1986, and 1988, and received a Star of People's Friendship in gold (second class) in October 1986 for her sporting achievements. Her career was affected by the exposure of widespread doping in East German athletics, with former teammate Petra Schneider admitting to using banned substances; however, Otto stated she was unaware of doping and passed all doping tests, asserting: "The medals are the only reminder of how hard I worked. It was not all drugs."
